name: Megillah Reading Times and Locations (Walled vs. Unwalled Cities)
notes: Laws governing when Megillah is read — 14th vs. 15th of Adar — based on whether a city was walled since the days of Joshua; includes advancing reading to day of assembly for villages

name: Walled Cities (Kerakin Mukafoot Chomah) — Purim on 15th
hebrew: כרכים המוקפין חומה מימות יהושע בן נון
notes: Definition and halakhic status of cities walled since Joshua's time, who read Megillah on the 15th of Adar

name: Day of Assembly (Yom HaKenisah) — Advancing Mitzvot
notes: Rabbinic enactment permitting villages to advance Megillah reading to Monday or Thursday (day of assembly/market day)

name: Gifts to the Poor on Purim (Matanot LaEvyonim)
notes: Obligation to distribute gifts to the poor on Purim; must be performed on actual Purim day even when Megillah reading is advanced

name: First and Second Adar (Adar Rishon v'Sheni) — Purim Timing
notes: Distinction between first and second Adar in a leap year regarding Megillah reading and Purim observance — Purim is in second Adar

name: Four Special Torah Portions (Arba Parshiyot)
notes: The four special Torah portions read on Shabbatot surrounding Adar: Shekalim, Zachor, Parah, HaChodesh

name: Parshat Shekalim
notes: Special Torah portion read on Shabbat of or before Rosh Chodesh Adar, relating to the half-shekel Temple tax

name: Parshat Zachor
notes: Special Torah portion read on the Shabbat before Purim; mitzva to remember/eradicate Amalek

name: Parshat Parah
notes: Special Torah portion about the Red Heifer read on the third special Shabbat, to prepare for Passover purity

name: Parshat HaChodesh
notes: Special Torah portion about the first month (Exodus 12) read on the fourth special Shabbat before Passover

name: Number of Torah Readers (Aliyot) by Day
notes: Rules governing the number of people called up to read Torah: 3 on Monday/Thursday/Shabbat Mincha, 4 on Rosh Chodesh/Chol HaMoed, 5 on Yom Tov, 6 on Yom Kippur, 7 on Shabbat

name: Laws of Haftarah Reading
notes: When haftarah is read, who reads it, skipping within Prophets, the person who reads haftarah also leads other parts of service

name: Blessings Before and After Torah Reading
notes: Who recites blessings before and after the Torah reading — first and last reader bless; middle readers do not

name: Minimum Verses in Torah Reading
notes: Each Torah reader must read a minimum of three verses; rules about reading to a translator one verse at a time

name: Aramaic Translation (Targum) During Torah Reading
notes: Rules about translating Torah and Prophets into Aramaic during public reading — one verse at a time for Torah, three for Prophets

name: Requirements of Ten for Sacred Matters (Davar shebKedushah)
notes: List of sacred activities requiring a minyan of ten: Shema blessings, prayer repetition, Priestly Blessing, Torah reading, haftarah, funeral rites, bridegroom's blessing, zimmun with God's name

name: Sanctity of Synagogue (Kedushat Beit Knesset)
notes: Halakhic sanctity of synagogues and their sale; restrictions on uses even in ruin; hierarchy of sacred objects

name: Sale of a Synagogue (Mechirat Beit Knesset)
notes: Rules governing the sale of a synagogue — conditions, permitted uses after sale, downgrading of sanctity prohibition

name: Hierarchy of Sacred Objects (Maalot HaKedushah)
hebrew: מעלות הקדושה — עולין בקודש ואין מורידין
notes: Principle of ascending in sanctity and not descending — proceeds from sale of sacred items may only purchase items of greater sanctity

name: Requirements for Writing the Megillah
notes: Megillah must be written in Ashurit (Hebrew script), on parchment, with ink; specific invalid writing materials listed

name: Requirements for Reading the Megillah (Keriat HaMegillah)
notes: Reading must be in order, not by heart, not in translation one doesn't understand; who is obligated and who may read; need for intent

name: Who is Fit to Read the Megillah
notes: All are fit to read except deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor (Rabbi Yehuda permits a minor); language requirements

name: All-Day Validity of Mitzvot (Kol HaYom Kasher)
notes: Principle that mitzvot of the day may be performed any time during the day; parallel principle for nighttime mitzvot

name: Prohibited Sections in Public Torah Reading and Translation
hebrew: סדרי קריאה — נקרא ולא מתורגם, לא נקרא ולא מתורגם
notes: Certain Torah passages (Reuben/Bilhah, second Golden Calf narrative, Priestly Benediction, David/Amnon) are read but not translated or neither read nor translated in public

name: Prohibition to Use Maaseh Merkavah as Haftarah
notes: Prohibition to conclude public Torah reading with the section of the Divine Chariot (Ezekiel 1); Rabbi Yehuda permits it

name: Qualifications of Prayer Leader (Shaliach Tzibbur)
notes: Who may lead public prayer — restrictions on those with exposed limbs, the blind (dispute), heretics; also covers Priestly Blessing eligibility

name: Heretical Prayer Formulations (Minim in Prayer)
notes: Prayers that indicate heretical belief — 'may the good bless You,' double 'we give thanks,' extending mercy of shiluach haken to all — are silenced

name: Shape and Placement of Tefillin
notes: Round tefillin are invalid; placement on forehead (not above hairline) or palm (not bicep) are ways of heretics; gold-plated or worn on outside of sleeve are ways of outsiders

name: Eligibility for Priestly Blessing (Birchat Kohanim — Who May Duchen)
notes: Priests with blemished or discolored hands, those who attract undue attention, may not duchen; rules about who performs the blessing in connection with Torah reading service

name: Passing Before the Ark (Maavar Lifnei HaTevah)
notes: Rules about who leads the repeated Amida prayer — connection to haftarah reader, restrictions on those in colored/no-sandal garments

name: Hakhel (Assembly of the Nation)
notes: Commandment for the king to read Deuteronomy before all Israel on Sukkot following the Sabbatical year; mentioned as an example of a mitzvah that is postponed rather than advanced

name: Non-Priestly Watches (Anshei Ma'amad)
notes: Representatives of the lay public who accompanied or fasted during the priestly watches; they read from Creation in the Torah; mentioned in context of special Torah reading occasions

name: Special Torah Portions for Holidays and Occasions
notes: The specific Torah portions assigned for each holiday: Passover, Shavuot, Rosh HaShanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Hanukkah, Purim, Rosh Chodesh, fast days

name: Zimmun with God's Name (Zimmun beShem with Ten)
notes: The elevated form of zimmun using God's name requires ten adult men present

name: Funeral Eulogy Rows and Comforting Mourners (Shurot Nichum Aveilim)
notes: Practice of mourners standing and community passing in rows to comfort them; requires a minyan of ten

name: Bridegroom's Blessing Requires Ten (Birchat Chatanim)
notes: The seven wedding blessings (sheva brachot) require a quorum of ten men

name: Language of Megillah Reading
notes: Foreign-language speakers may hear Megillah in their language; one who hears it in Hebrew (Ashurit) fulfills obligation regardless of language; reading by heart or in unknown language does not fulfill obligation

name: Bull of Anointed Kohen Gadol for Erroneous Ruling
hebrew: פר כהן משיח על שגגת הוראה
notes: The anointed (oil) High Priest brings a special bull if he issued an erroneous ruling and acted upon it; the multi-garment High Priest does not bring this offering

name: Halakhic Distinction of Walled vs. Unwalled in Various Contexts
hebrew: הבדל בין מוקף חומה לשאינו מוקף חומה
notes: The concept of walled cities (from Joshua's time) appears in multiple halakhic contexts: Purim reading, eating consecrated food near Shiloh/Jerusalem, redemption of houses
